claims.statement: The block chains run in a 48 kHz chain domain: kChainBaseSampleRate = 48000.0 in ChainDomain.h, and the effective chain rate is that times the current oversampling factor (TONE3000Processor::chainSampleRate).

The host-rate to chain-rate boundary is a stereo Lanczos resampler (filter size 12, dsp::ResamplingContainer<float,2,12>) that is only instantiated when the host rate differs from 48 kHz, so 48 kHz hosts see a passthrough.

Boundary plus oversampler/pitch-shift latency is reported to the host on the message thread; a powered-off plugin stays bit-exact and zero-latency; a mono host buffer gets a second silent channel since the boundary is a fixed 2-channel container.

ChainBlock.h defines the block universe: ChainBlockType { NAM, IR, INSERT, EFFECT }, EffectKind { Delay, Chorus, Tremolo, Compressor, Reverb, Convolution }, ChainSide { Left, Right }, plus kMinLaneSlots=5 (an empty lane shows 5 slots), kWetFadeSeconds=0.025, and kIrConvolverMaxBlockSize=256.

processConvolverInChunks splits the host stream into <=256-frame chunks to feed the JUCE convolver, bounding the per-call cost of its non-uniform OLA tail; hosts at or below the cap get exactly the raw block.

RtWorkerPool is a realtime fork/join pool with nesting depth 1 (a lane job can fork its NAM block's phases); it is deadlock-free by construction because a joiner never parks — it claims and runs its jobs inline, stealing work back if every worker is descheduled or busy.

RtWorkerPool workers run at realtime priority (falling back to normal highest-priority threads if RT start is refused) and, when the host provides one, join the audio thread's workgroup context, re-joining whenever it changes (tokens are thread-affine) to stay off efficiency cores; wakeups are precise (parked workers advertise themselves), not broadcast.

Block swaps, model downloads and preset splices are audio-thread splices: ProcessorChain fades with the 25 ms wet fade where a single block can fade, or performs a mute-splice of the whole chain output where no single block can fade (e.g. removing a running chain).
